predecessors.name: County of Barcelona
predecessors.text: Besalú, 'roughly coterminous with the modern comarca of Garrotxa'

successors.name: County of Barcelona
successors.text: the county itself, inherited by Barcelona when Bernard III died in 1111

successors.name: County of Berga
successors.text: Vallespir, Fenolledès, Peyrepertuse and Castellnou, 'ceded to Cerdanya as compensation'

rulers.name: Miro I the Younger (Miró II of Cerdanya)

ledger.x: 878: Wilfred the Hairy cedes Besalú to his brother Radulf, who becomes its first count.
912: Miró II of Cerdanya takes Besalú, which is drawn with Cerdanya-Berga until 927.
927: Miró II dies and Besalú passes to Wilfred II under the regency of Ava.
957: after a revolt of the nobles Sunifred of Cerdanya takes over Besalú.
988: Oliba Cabreta enters Montecassino and leaves Besalú, Vallespir, Fenouillèdes and Peyrepertuse to Bernard Tallaferro, who founds an independent line.
1111: Bernard III dies and Barcelona inherits Besalú.
1111: Vallespir, Fenolledès, Peyrepertuse and Castellnou go to Cerdanya as compensation.

wars.name: Revolt of 957 in Besalú
wars.outcome: Wilfred (II) was assassinated and Sunifred of Cerdanya took over the county; in 965 he passed his counties to Oliba.

wars.name: Dispute over the inheritance of Besalú (1111)
wars.outcome: Barcelona kept Besalú itself; Bernard William of Cerdanya, Besalú's feudal suzerain, received the four trans-Pyrenean districts as compensation.

certainty.note: Comital frontiers follow the pagi and castles; no treaty or survey line is given.

sources.title: Ramon Berenguer III, Count of Barcelona
